scope: Mirror-only CPU material workshop using the standalone OGC adaptation; original solver, benchmark scale and assets are not reproduced.

cases.description: Worker · Dig a ground section
cases.differences: Shared gameplay tools, materials and OGC. Player mesh with two-hand/leg IK and reduced muscle actuators; supported torso motion is prescribed. No forced excavation. Physical and visual results await user playtest.

cases.description: Worker · Chop a standing tree
cases.differences: Same anchored grain-bearing tree model as gameplay, with a visible supported worker and finite-force axe grips. No forced felling. Physical and visual results await user playtest.

cases.description: Worker · Shovel and compact snow
cases.differences: Compressible plastic APIC snow with OGC boundaries and a supported shoveling worker. Meltwater preserves parcel mass. Heating is labelled at 180x; physical motion is ordinary speed. Awaiting user playtest.

cases.description: Ice · Fracture, float and melt in warm water
cases.differences: Brittle bonded ice, exact clipped-volume buoyancy and a finite hydrostatic warm-water reservoir. Cellwise latent-heat melting at labelled 240x thermal time; mechanics run at ordinary speed. No resolved waves or refreezing. Awaiting user playtest.

cases.description: Ice · Melt in air
cases.differences: Same ice material in warm air, with meltwater transferred into explicit APIC/OGC parcels. Labelled 240x thermal time; coarse cellwise melt front, no refreezing. Awaiting user playtest.

cases.description: Dirt — curved spade and adaptive loam
cases.differences: Adaptive meshfree material, plastic loam, cohesive failure, implicit display skin and finite-force OGC spade contact. Compile-checked; user playtest pending.

cases.description: Turf — rooted sod, spade cut and peel
cases.differences: Established turf has a dedicated deformable prism mesh, volume constraints, separate soil seams and tensile root bundles. 384 crowns and 1536 attached blade meshes follow the mat. Edge work cuts roots; tensile overload tears them permanently. OGC contacts the actual mat and spade. Individual leaf dynamics and biological growth remain in the separate seedling experiment. Uncalibrated reduced material.

cases.description: Seedlings — retained germination experiment
cases.differences: Retained former grass demonstration: accelerated seed/growth state with moisture and reserves, roots in adaptive loam and OGC shoot/tool contact. This is sparse germination, not established turf.

cases.description: Fine sand — frictional continuum and bucket
cases.differences: APIC material points represent parcels of fine dry sand. Hencky elastic strain and Drucker-Prager plastic yielding provide pressure-dependent shear resistance without tensile cohesion. Accepted OGC boundary motion updates strain. Continuous display skin; individual microscopic grains are not explicitly simulated. Bounded workshop patch, not a full beach.

cases.description: Pebbles — retained discrete grains and bucket
cases.differences: The former matter_sand model is retained unchanged as pebbles: fixed centimetre-scale closed grain surfaces and persistent Coulomb contact constraints. No grain subdivision.

cases.description: Wood — axe split along grain
cases.differences: Game-generated cut trunk on the contact table. Continuous fibre bundles are stiff; the weaker matrix between them fails at finite critical opening. Fracture fronts propagate along weak grain planes using contact work and axe orientation. Broken connections cannot act as elastic tethers. Prepared interfaces set fracture resolution.

cases.description: Wood — axe chop across grain
cases.differences: Same trunk and material as the splitting case. A sideways axe stroke loads the cross-grain fibres. Cross-grain interfaces require local cutting-edge contact and greater strength/toughness than longitudinal cleavage.

cases.description: Stone — pick and brittle fracture
cases.differences: A closed angular rock with shape-preserving convex cells and traction/work-driven brittle interfaces. Tip contact area controls stress. Light tap then stronger pick blows. Chips preserve geometry, volume and mass.

cases.description: Loose stone — curved shovel
cases.differences: Separate closed stones lifted through OGC shovel contact. Shovel proximity never subdivides a stone; actual stress/work must fracture its material interfaces.

cases.description: Stone — broad bucket contact comparison
cases.differences: The same rock and fracture law as the pick scene. A bucket applies the same sequence of drive-force limits over its broader contact surface; no tool-name damage exception exists.

cases.description: Dirt — compare light / medium / strong force
cases.differences: Three fresh deterministic specimens, 17 seconds each. Identical requested trajectories and tool mass; actuator force limits 45, 240 and 800 N. Reports actual contact force, head kinetic energy, contact work, fracture and lifted/contained matter. Drive limit is not measured impact force. Reset restarts all trials.

cases.description: Layered ground — turf, soil, shovel and bedrock
cases.differences: One coupled OGC scene: rooted turf over cohesive soil over brittle rock. Root anchors transfer load between turf and soil. Repeated shovel scoops deposit existing material beside the hole; a pick is selected only when a clear bedrock patch is measured. Remaining cover is reported honestly. No timed removal, material reset or forced attachment. Fixed bounded section; approximately one to two minutes depending on excavation.

cases.description: Soil and spade: contact and hold (Mirror experiment)
cases.origin: Mirror experiment, not an OGC paper benchmark
cases.differences: A force-driven compliant spade presses against a fixed-base deformable soil patch through OGC. Fracture, roots, detached soil and mobile controls are not implemented; physical parameters are uncalibrated.

cases.description: Automatic soil fracture and excavation (Mirror experiment)
cases.origin: Mirror experiment, not an OGC paper benchmark
cases.differences: 108 prepartitioned elastic soil cells, co-rotating cohesive interfaces damaged by tensile/shear load, a finite-force tapered spade and OGC contact. Numerical gaps and fixed cell-scale crack paths; uncalibrated material. Automatic press, lever, lift and tip; no forced debris attachment or deletion. Shaft and grass are visual geometry.

validation: Penetration/intersection check after every frame; halt on failure
Actual simulated time per wall-clock second
Declared differences in mesh, solver, hardware and scale
Current monitor is discrete; it does not establish continuous collision detection or friction/thread pull-through correctness.
Every failed candidate restores the previous valid geometry and retries a smaller step; the run halts if the minimum step is rejected.
